title: Interim: borrow the serial port for flashing under conserver
description: Until OTA lands, conserver and espflash both want /dev/ttyUSB0 exclusively. Provide flash-under-conserver.sh (stop or down conserver, espflash flash, restore) wired as the cargo runner or a make target so cargo run transparently borrows the port; document conserver native down/up (Ctrl-E c d then o) as the lighter alternative. Superseded by the OTA epic once flashing no longer needs the UART.

title: NightDriver-style WS2812 LED driver as an HA light
description: Second product on the shared foundation: a NightDriverStrip-inspired WS2812 effects driver for the workstation, exposed to Home Assistant as a Light entity (on/off, brightness, effect-select) through the same esphome-api framework. The existing led-core effects domain (color, effect, animator) is reused unchanged; under the std pivot the WS2812 adapter re-homes from esp-hal RMT to esp-idf-hal RMT. This epic proves the generic native-API entity framework pays off a second time: swap the adapter and expose a Light instead of a Sensor. Depends on the foundation (std pivot, workspace, esphome-api).

title: led-driver bin: drive the WS2812 strip as an HA Light
description: The project #2 application binary: a composition root that drives the led-core effects through the re-homed WS2812 adapter and exposes the strip to Home Assistant as a Light entity (on/off, brightness, effect-select) via the esphome-api framework and the firmware-infra native-API server. Under Functional Core / Imperative Shell the animator returns a rendered frame value and the adapter (shell) writes it. Acceptance: HA shows a Light entity that toggles, dims, and switches effects on the physical strip. Depends on the WS2812 encoder, the Light entity type, and the native-API server infra.

title: esphome-api: add Light entity type to the registry
description: Extend the generic esphome-api entity model with a Light entity (on/off, brightness, effect-select): add the ListEntitiesLight, LightState, and LightCommand messages to the enums and implement a LightEntity mapping to led-core effect selection and brightness, including handle_command for inbound LightCommandRequest. Proves the framework generalizes beyond read-only Sensor. Tests: registry emits Light List/State; a LightCommand routes to the entity by key. Depends on the generic entity model.

title: std/ESP-IDF foundation + ESPHome-native plant monitor
description: Foundation plus first product. Pivot the M5StickC Plus firmware from no_std esp-hal to std on ESP-IDF (esp-idf-svc, esp-idf-hal, esp-idf-sys), then ship a soil-moisture plant monitor that appears to Home Assistant as a native ESPHome device (protobuf over TCP 6053 plus mDNS) so HA stores, graphs and alerts on the readings. Board is ESP32-PICO-D4 (4MB flash, 520KB SRAM, no PSRAM), which runs std comfortably. Why std: it turns the ESPHome native API into a roughly one-week job instead of weeks (std::net TCP, prost protobuf, ESP-IDF WiFi/mDNS/OTA, pure-Rust Noise) and it also simplifies OTA. Domain crates (led-core, plant-core, the esphome-api protocol core) stay pure and framework-free. Architecture: hexagonal/ECB plus Functional Core / Imperative Shell (Bernhardt Boundaries) plus dogfooding the ~/code/tools contract suite (hex-lint, effect-audit, cargo-regime-check) as the CI gates that enforce both. This epic reverses and supersedes the no_std OTA epic stick-c-plus-qqh (ESP-IDF supplies WiFi/OTA/mDNS natively). MVP milestone is the plaintext native-API sensor entity graphing in HA. Full design saved at docs/plans/plant-monitor-esphome-native-api.md.

title: Stand up the std/ESP-IDF build and boot
description: Get the firmware crate building and BOOTING on std ESP-IDF, nothing more. Target xtensa-esp32-espidf on the esp toolchain; add esp-idf-svc 0.52, esp-idf-hal 0.46, esp-idf-sys 0.37; linker via ldproxy; build-std = std,panic_abort; build.rs uses embuild sysenv output; add sdkconfig.defaults (larger main-task and pthread stacks, more lwIP sockets, mDNS max services, size optimization); pin ESP_IDF_VERSION to a 5.3.x tag (esp-idf-sys 0.37 needs at least 5.3.0). Drop esp-hal, esp-backtrace, esp-println. Runner stays espflash flash --monitor; ELF path becomes target/xtensa-esp32-espidf. SCOPE: only a minimal std binary that boots and logs over serial. Re-homing the WS2812 and Clock adapters and the workspace split are separate beads. Acceptance: a minimal std ESP-IDF binary flashes and logs on the board. Open item: confirm the exact 5.3.x tag esp-idf-sys 0.37 targets.

title: Noise encryption follow-on for the native API
description: Add the Noise transport so the native API is encrypted, matching current ESPHome direction (2026.1 removed API password auth in favor of encryption). Reuse the UbiHome noise-protocol plus noise-rust-crypto responder (no_std-capable, no tokio): Noise_NNpsk0_25519_ChaChaPoly_SHA256, PSK is the base64 32-byte HA key, device is the responder; feature-gate so plaintext builds omit it. Advertise api_encryption in the mDNS TXT when on. On the HA side, paste the same base64 key into the ESPHome integration. Acceptance: HA connects with encryption enabled using the shared key; a wrong key is rejected. Open items: confirm noise-protocol/noise-rust-crypto cross-compile on xtensa-esp32-espidf; verify the Noise inner-frame layout against aioesphomeapi connection.py.

title: Stand up Home Assistant on the LAN
description: Home Assistant is the store-and-graph plane for every project and is not yet running. Stand up an instance on the LAN: HAOS on a mini-PC, Pi, or VM is recommended; HA Container (Docker) also works but must use host networking or macvlan so mDNS discovery works on the same L2. No MQTT or Mosquitto needed on the native-API path. SCOPE: only a reachable HA; adopting the device is a separate bead. Acceptance: HA is reachable on the LAN. Can start immediately, independent of the firmware.

title: ESP-IDF OTA slot mechanism (EspOta: write, flip, rollback)
description: The OTA mechanism on ESP-IDF: use esp-idf-svc EspOta to write an image into the inactive OTA slot, mark it, reboot into it, and roll back on a failed boot. ESP-IDF supplies the partition, otadata, and bootloader machinery natively (why this supersedes the whole no_std OTA stack the old qqh epic pinned). SCOPE: only the local slot mechanism (image source may be an embedded blob or flash read here); the network fetch and update policy are a separate bead. Acceptance: an image is written to the inactive slot, booted, and a deliberately bad image rolls back, on the board. Depends on the std build and the workspace.

title: Pin ESPHome/ESP-IDF reference sources to kb/sources
description: Save the reference material offline (user request) as pinned kb/sources entries (commit/tag pinned submodules or fetched datasheets): UbiHome/esphome-native-api plus its encryption doc; aioesphomeapi (the api.proto source and connection.py Noise oracle); a note that esphome/esphome components/api is GPLv3 and reference-only; ESPHome native-API protocol details; HA ESPHome integration and security/Noise pages; the Rust-on-ESP std book, esp-idf-template, esp-idf-sys build options; esp-idf-svc and esp-idf-hal docs; prost, noise-protocol, noise-rust-crypto and the Noise NNpsk0 spec; mipidsi, embedded-graphics and the ST7789 datasheet; axp192 and the AXP192 datasheet; the Earth Unit datasheet. SCOPE: pinning sources only; writing the derived findings is a separate bead. Depends on the vendored crate being chosen.

title: Tag crates with hex-arch roles + wire hex-lint gate
description: Tag every workspace crate with package.metadata.hex-arch role (domain / driven-adapter / infra / composition-root) and optional context (led / plant / api), then wire the hex-lint gate (from ~/code/tools) into the justfile and pre-commit/CI. It fails any cross-role dependency edge, for example the ESPHome transport or the ADC HAL sneaking into a role=domain crate. Advisory first, then blocking; follow the suite exit-code contract 0 clean / 1 policy violation / 2 tool error. Also adopt the suite house style: forbid unsafe on our crates, clippy deny-all, cucumber specs. SCOPE: role tagging plus hex-lint only; effect-audit and cargo-regime-check are separate beads. Depends on the workspace skeleton.

title: Re-home the Clock adapter to std/ESP-IDF time
description: Re-implement the led-core Clock port adapter (currently EspClock over the esp-hal monotonic timer) on ESP-IDF time (esp-idf-hal or std Instant), returning elapsed Duration from boot. Small shell adapter in the adapters crate. Under Functional Core / Imperative Shell the shell reads the clock and passes the value into the domain. Acceptance: the animator/sampler receives correct monotonic time on the board. Depends on the std build and the workspace skeleton.

title: plant-core: SoilSensor port + pure sampler step
description: Add to plant-core the driven port SoilSensor (associated Error, read_raw returning 0..=4095) and the PURE Control step: given previous state, a slice of raw readings, and Calibration, average, calibrate (via to_percent), and return the new state plus whether the value changed. No sensor handle, no caching, no I/O in the core. Tests: unit tests with a scripted-sensor fake (zero/one/many readings); a cucumber feature moisture.feature (given calibration and a reading, then a percent). effect-audit must pass with role=domain. Depends on the Moisture/calibration bead. Pure host work.

title: esphome-api: blocking frame codec over std::io
description: Implement the ESPHome native-API frame codec as a blocking reader/writer over std::io Read and Write, replacing the vendored tokio-util codec. Plaintext frame = 1-byte preamble 0x00, then varint payload length, then payload (varint message-type-id, varint length, protobuf). Encrypted frames (preamble 0x01, 2-byte big-endian length) are handled by the Noise bead. Pure, no sockets. Tests: round-trip encode/decode across message lengths; malformed and short-read handling. Depends on the vendored crate and proto types.

title: esphome-api: generic entity model (ApiEntity + Registry + Sensor)
description: Define the generic entity abstraction: an ApiEntity trait (key, object_id, list_message, state_message, handle_command) and a Registry holding boxed entities, with List/State/Command enums covering every ESPHome entity type (Sensor, BinarySensor, Switch, Light, Number, Select, Cover). Implement SensorEntity now; other types are enum variants added later without rewrite. Pure. Tests: registry enumerates List and State messages for a Sensor; key hashing is stable. Depends on the vendored crate and proto types.

title: esphome-api: pure connection FSM + host value-tests
description: Implement the native-API connection as a PURE function of state and inbound message: handle(conn, inbound, entity-snapshot) returns (new-conn, outbound-messages). Cover Hello, DeviceInfo, ListEntities plus ListEntitiesDone, SubscribeStates then stream states, Ping/Pong, Disconnect. No sockets. Tests (Functional Core, no network, no mocks): feed inbound frames as values and assert the outbound sequence and every entity List/State message; include an integration test that binds 127.0.0.1 and drives the real aioesphomeapi client as a conformance oracle. effect-audit must pass with role=domain. Depends on the codec and the entity model.

title: Carve the firmware into a multi-crate workspace
description: Split the firmware into a workspace of small single-responsibility crates so the hexagon and Functional-Core/Imperative-Shell boundaries become enforceable per crate. New members: board-support (M5StickC Plus BSP, reused by all projects); firmware-infra (WiFi, mDNS, the native-API socket server host, OTA; reused by all projects); adapters (domain-port adapters: adc, st7789, wifi, clock, ws2812); bins/plant-monitor (first binary and composition root). Shared host crates (led-core, plant-core, esphome-api) referenced by path. Move the existing composition root into bins/plant-monitor. SCOPE: only the crate skeleton and moving existing code in. The hex-arch role tags and the CI gates are a separate bead. Acceptance: the workspace builds and the layout matches the design. Depends on the std build.

title: AXP192 power-on (board-support): enable LCD/TFT rails
description: In the board-support crate, bring up the internal I2C bus (SDA GPIO21, SCL GPIO22) and power the AXP192 PMIC rails the board needs: LDO2 (LCD backlight) and LDO3 (TFT), plus the standard M5StickC Plus init register writes to address 0x34. Load-bearing prerequisite for the display; reused by every project. Share the one I2C bus via embedded-hal-bus (AXP192 now, MPU6886/RTC later). Acceptance: the backlight powers on and the AXP192 reports the expected rail voltages. Depends on the std build and the workspace skeleton.

title: Sampler shell thread: ADC to plant-core step to shared Moisture
description: The imperative-shell sampler: a sized std::thread that periodically reads the ADC adapter, runs the pure plant-core sampler step, and publishes the latest Moisture into a shared Arc Mutex that the display and the native-API server read. Owns the timing and the cache (the core stays pure). Acceptance: the shared latest-Moisture updates on the board as the probe wets and dries. Depends on the ADC adapter and the pure sampler step.

title: Adopt the device in HA + moisture graph + watering alert
description: With Home Assistant running and the device serving the native API, adopt it: accept the mDNS discovery or add the ESPHome integration by IP on port 6053 (plaintext: no key; Noise: paste the base64 key). Confirm the Soil Moisture entity records history and graphs. Add a watering-alert automation that fires when the moisture entity crosses a low threshold. Acceptance: the entity graphs in HA History and the alert fires on a dry reading. Depends on standing up HA and the on-device server MVP.

title: OTA image fetch + update use case (HTTP pull, policy, trigger)
description: On top of the OTA slot mechanism, add the update use case: fetch a firmware image over WiFi (HTTP pull from a homelab URL) and drive the slot write/flip/rollback. Model the update policy (whether/when to update, version check) in the domain and the HTTP transport as an adapter. Acceptance: an image served from the homelab is pulled and booted end to end. Depends on the OTA slot mechanism and WiFi. Once this lands, the interim serial-borrow bead stick-c-plus-5ww is retired and the UART can host a permanent shared console.

title: Write kb/findings for the pivot, native API, Noise, Earth Unit, pin map
description: Write the derived KB findings (one falsifiable fact per file): the std/ESP-IDF pivot that supersedes the no_std OTA stack (cross-link the esp-rs version matrix); the ESPHome native-API framing plus message-type-id table plus connection flow; the ESPHome Noise parameters (NNpsk0_25519_ChaChaPoly_SHA256, device is responder); the Earth Unit capacitive probe on ADC1 channel 5 (G33) with dry/wet calibration and the ADC1-for-WiFi-coexistence rule; the M5StickC Plus std-ESP-IDF pin map. Depends on the MVP server so the findings reflect verified behavior.

title: Wire effect-audit --require-domain over the domain crates
description: Add the effect-audit gate (from ~/code/tools) to the justfile and pre-commit/CI over the Functional-Core crates led-core, plant-core, and the esphome-api core. It fails the instant a clock, RNG, ADC handle, socket, tokio, or mutable-static leaks into a role=domain crate. Use --require-domain as the anti-false-green guard (a run that audited nothing exits 2). Advisory first, then blocking. Feedback loop: effect-audit is the least-productized of the six tools, so leaning on it here will surface and harden its rough edges. Depends on the hex-arch role tagging and the domain crates existing.

title: Wire cargo-regime-check on the reusable library crates
description: Add the cargo-regime-check gate (from ~/code/tools) over the reusable library crates led-core, plant-core, and esphome-api, so a change claiming to be just a refactor is mechanically falsifiable against the declared public-API transition (needs cargo public-api on nightly piped in). Overkill for leaf binaries, so scope it to the libs. Depends on the hex-arch role tagging and the library crates existing.

title: firmware-infra: reusable native-API server host (accept loop)
description: The reusable imperative-shell server that BOTH the plant monitor and the LED driver build on: in firmware-infra, a blocking TcpListener on 0.0.0.0:6053 (cap 1 to 2 connections, no PSRAM) that accepts connections and pumps bytes through the pure esphome-api connection FSM, serving whatever entities the composition root registers. No entity-specific or project-specific logic here. Acceptance: a host or on-device test connects with aioesphomeapi and completes the handshake, list-entities, and subscribe against a test registry. Depends on the connection FSM and the workspace skeleton.

title: Walking-skeleton spike: esp-idf std to WiFi to TCP:6053 to mDNS to HA adopts a plaintext device
description: THROWAWAY vertical slice to convert the plan riskiest unknowns into facts BEFORE building the clean architecture. A single-file esp-idf std binary: join WiFi, run a blocking TcpListener on 6053, advertise _esphomelib._tcp via the ESP-IDF mDNS component, and answer the ESPHome native-API PLAINTEXT handshake (Hello, DeviceInfo, ListEntities, SubscribeStates) exposing ONE hardcoded Sensor value, using the vendored UbiHome prost types and a codec sketch. Acceptance: a real Home Assistant instance discovers and adopts the device over plaintext and shows the hardcoded sensor updating (and/or the aioesphomeapi client completes the same flow). Proves in one shot: esp-idf std builds and boots, WiFi plus DHCP, the mDNS managed-component wiring, the plaintext framing/handshake, that current HA accepts an unencrypted device (else Noise becomes MVP-blocking), and rough RAM/stack fit on the 520KB PICO-D4. Findings feed the real beads; the code is discarded. Depends on the std build and a running HA.

title: Soil calibration: capture dry/wet points + persist to NVS
description: Make the moisture percent MEANINGFUL. Capacitive probes vary per unit and drift, so dry_raw/wet_raw must be captured per probe, not hardcoded. Add a device-side calibration flow: capture a dry reading (probe in air/dry soil) and a wet reading (probe in water/wet soil), triggered by a button or a Home Assistant Button/Number entity, and persist the Calibration to ESP-IDF NVS so it survives reboot; the sampler reads the persisted calibration. The raw MVP may ship with hardcoded constants; this refines it into a usable monitor. Acceptance: after a dry-then-wet capture, the reported percent reads about 0 in dry air and about 100 in water, and the calibration survives a power cycle. Depends on the Moisture/calibration types and the ADC adapter.

title: plant-core: Moisture entity + calibration (pure)
description: Start the no_std, zero-dependency plant-core crate with the value types only: Moisture, a u8 newtype with invariant 0..=100, and Calibration (dry_raw, wet_raw), plus to_percent(raw, cal) using integer-only i32 math (no float, no libm), clamped and branch-safe for either calibration order (capacitive probes read higher when dry). Tests: property tests proving the result is always in 0..=100, dry_raw maps to 0, wet_raw maps to 100, monotonicity, out-of-range clamps. The SoilSensor port and the sampler step are a separate bead. effect-audit must pass with role=domain. Pure host work; start immediately.

title: Pre-implementation polish + cross-model review of the bead graph
description: Plan-space is cheaper than build-space. Before implementing, run the beads-workflow polish loop (several rounds) plus at least one cross-model review over the whole graph: sharpen priorities so P1 marks only the MVP spine (currently nearly everything is P1), add rough time estimates so bv critical-path/slack analysis is meaningful, move done-conditions into the structured acceptance-criteria field, defer the rover epic so it stops surfacing as actionable, and sanity-check every dependency edge and single-responsibility scope. Acceptance: priorities differentiated, estimates set on the spine, acceptance-criteria populated on the MVP beads, rover deferred, and a second model has reviewed the graph with no unresolved objections. Ready now; do it before starting the build.

title: esphome-api: vendor UbiHome + api.proto + prost types
description: Stand up the esphome-api crate by vendoring/forking UbiHome/esphome-native-api (MIT) locally. Lift the api.proto (take it from aioesphomeapi, MIT; never from esphome/esphome which is GPLv3), the prost message types, and the message-type-id registry; strip the tokio surface so the crate builds on the host with no async runtime. SCOPE: vendor plus proto/types/id-registry only. The codec, the entity model, and the connection FSM are separate beads. Acceptance: the crate builds on the host and exposes the prost types and the id registry. Open items: confirm UbiHome ships committed prost .rs (no build-time protoc), enable exactly one api-version feature, confirm noise-rust license is MIT-compatible. Pure host work.

title: ADC adapter: SoilSensor over ADC1 on GPIO33
description: Shell adapter implementing the plant-core SoilSensor port over the ESP-IDF oneshot ADC. Read the Earth Unit analog capacitive output on GPIO33, which is ADC1 channel 5. MUST be ADC1, because ADC2 is unusable while WiFi is active. Use esp-idf-hal AdcDriver on ADC1 plus an AdcChannelDriver on gpio33 with 12 dB attenuation; oversample and average. Error type is EspError. The digital threshold line on GPIO32 is optional and could later back a BinarySensor entity. Confirmed by the vendor Earth example in the repo which does analogRead(33). Acceptance: on the board, moisture readings track a probe moved between dry air, dry soil, and wet soil, and stay stable when oversampled. Open item: whether esp-idf-hal 0.46 exposes ADC line/curve calibration on ESP32 (raw counts are adequate for relative moisture regardless).

title: ST7789 display adapter (mipidsi) + render moisture
description: Drive the onboard ST7789 TFT (135x240) via mipidsi over display-interface-spi on SPI pins MOSI 15, SCLK 13, DC 23, RST 18, CS 5; apply the M5StickC Plus column/row offset and the panel inversion (INVON) or the image renders shifted and wrong-colored. Render the current moisture percent with embedded-graphics. Lives in the adapters crate. Requires the AXP192 rails powered first (separate bead). Optional for the MVP; can be deferred. Acceptance: the moisture percent is legible on the screen and updates. Open item: verify the exact ST7789 offset and inversion against a known-good M5StickC Plus mipidsi example.

title: WiFi STA bring-up via esp-idf-svc
description: Join the 2.4 GHz network as a station and obtain a DHCP lease using esp-idf-svc EspWifi wrapped in BlockingWifi, Client configuration. Credentials MUST NOT be committed: read SSID and password from a git-ignored firmware/secrets.toml consumed at build time (build.rs emits them as env, read via env). Add secrets.toml and the Noise PSK file to gitignore. Lives in firmware-infra (shell). Acceptance: the board logs an acquired IP and resolves DNS. Supersedes the no_std esp-radio WiFi work (was stick-c-plus-qqh.3).

title: mDNS advertiser for _esphomelib._tcp
description: Advertise the device on the LAN so Home Assistant auto-discovers it as an ESPHome device. Use the ESP-IDF mDNS component via esp-idf-svc EspMdns: set hostname and instance name, add service _esphomelib over _tcp on port 6053 with TXT records (friendly_name, version, mac, platform, board, network=wifi, and api_encryption=Noise_NNpsk0_25519_ChaChaPoly_SHA256 once Noise is on). Lives in firmware-infra (shell). Acceptance: the device shows up in an mDNS browse for _esphomelib._tcp and HA raises a discovery notification. Open item: confirm the exact managed-component wiring (espressif/mdns) for esp-idf-svc 0.52.

title: Wire the plant Sensor entity into the server host (MVP)
description: The MVP milestone. On top of the reusable native-API server host, register a single Sensor entity (name Soil Moisture, unit percent, device_class moisture, state_class measurement, accuracy_decimals 0) whose state reads the shared latest Moisture from the sampler shell, and stand up the plant-monitor composition root (bins/plant-monitor) bringing up ADC, WiFi, mDNS, the sampler thread, and the server host. Plaintext first. Acceptance: with HA on the LAN, the Soil Moisture entity is adopted, updates as the probe wets and dries, and graphs in History; validated on the host against the aioesphomeapi oracle first. Depends on the server host, the sampler shell, WiFi, and mDNS. Open item: confirm current HA still accepts a plaintext native-API device.

title: OTA-over-WiFi firmware updates
description: Give the M5StickC Plus firmware-update-over-WiFi so flashing no longer needs exclusive ownership of /dev/ttyUSB0, which collides with a shared serial console (conserver). Board is confirmed capable: ESP32-PICO-D4, 2.4GHz WiFi, 4MB flash; the factory partition table already carries otadata and the ESP-IDF second-stage bootloader honors A/B OTA slots. Target stack pinned to latest (mid-2026): esp-hal 1.1, esp-radio (WiFi, successor to esp-wifi), esp-rtos (scheduler, successor to esp-hal-embassy), esp-storage plus esp-bootloader-esp-idf (flash writes plus otadata/rollback), embassy-net (TCP). Endgame: images push over the network into the inactive OTA slot and the UART is freed for a permanent shared console. led-core stays framework-free; OTA is a new use case behind ports. See the KB finding on the esp-rs version/compat matrix.
close_reason: Superseded by stick-c-plus-qhw: std/ESP-IDF pivot; ESP-IDF supplies WiFi/OTA/mDNS. qqh.1 kept and re-filed under the LED-driver epic; qqh.2-6 superseded.

title: Own the in-tree WS2812 RMT encoder (re-home to esp-idf RMT)
description: Own an in-tree WS2812 RMT encoder implementing the led-core LedOutput adapter, replacing esp-hal-smartled and smart-leds, with unchanged WS2812 datasheet timings. NOTE: the original esp-hal 1.1 substrate is superseded by the std/ESP-IDF pivot; the encoder now re-homes onto esp-idf-hal RMT (TxRmtDriver, FixedLengthSignal). The in-tree encoder concept and timings survive; only the RMT backend changes. Re-filed under the LED-driver project. Under Functional Core / Imperative Shell the animator returns a rendered frame value and this adapter writes it (the adapter is the shell). Acceptance: the strip renders correctly on the board with on-wire timing confirmed, not just a clean build.

title: Async runtime: esp-rtos executor + esp-alloc heap
description: WiFi and embassy-net are async and need an executor and a heap. Stand up esp-rtos (features esp32, embassy, esp-radio) as the scheduler -- it supersedes esp-hal-embassy, which is frozen on the 1.0 line -- and esp-alloc for the global allocator. Convert the blocking render loop into an embassy task on embassy-time (a 20ms tick), keeping led-core synchronous and untouched. Acceptance: builds and the LED animation still runs under the executor on the board.
close_reason: Superseded by the std/ESP-IDF pivot (stick-c-plus-qhw.1, stick-c-plus-qhw.2): ESP-IDF provides FreeRTOS and std, so no esp-rtos executor or esp-alloc heap is needed.

title: WiFi STA bring-up via esp-radio
description: Join a 2.4GHz AP as a station and obtain a DHCP lease via embassy-net, using esp-radio (features wifi, esp-alloc; needs the esp-rtos rtos-driver). Credentials must not be committed -- read from build-time env or a git-ignored config. Acceptance: the board logs an acquired IP and resolves DNS. Needs the board and AP credentials.
close_reason: Superseded by stick-c-plus-qhw.7: WiFi STA via esp-idf-svc EspWifi replaces the esp-radio bring-up.

title: Dual-OTA partition table + otadata/slot writer
description: Adopt firmware/partitions.csv (dual ota_0/ota_1, 4MB) via espflash --partition-table and update the runner/flash docs. Use esp-bootloader-esp-idf to read the partition table and otadata (active slot, mark valid/invalid for rollback) and esp-storage to write the inactive slot. Acceptance: read the current boot slot at runtime and write-plus-verify an image into the other slot on the board (image may come from a flash read or embedded blob at this stage; no network yet). Flashing this table overwrites the factory app -- factory image is backed up in KB.
close_reason: Superseded by stick-c-plus-qhw.12: ESP-IDF supplies partition/otadata/bootloader natively; no esp-storage or esp-bootloader-esp-idf slot writer needed.

title: OTA update use case: fetch image, flip slot, roll back on failure
description: The update flow as a domain use case. Add a port for the firmware-image source and a control (FirmwareUpdate) that fetches an image over embassy-net (HTTP pull from a homelab URL), streams it into the inactive OTA slot, validates it, sets otadata to boot the new slot, and reboots; a failed boot rolls back via the bootloader. The transport is an adapter; the update policy (whether/when to update, version check) lives in the domain. Acceptance: an image served from the homelab is pulled and booted end-to-end, and a deliberately-bad image rolls back.
close_reason: Superseded by stick-c-plus-qhw.12: OTA use case now uses esp-idf-svc EspOta (HTTP pull, slot flip, rollback).

title: OTA runbook + KB; free the UART for a permanent console
description: Document how to build and publish an OTA image, trigger an update, and verify/observe it (partition map, otadata semantics, rollback) as a KB guide plus finding. Once OTA is the update path, wire the permanent shared serial console (conserver owns /dev/ttyUSB0 for good) and update kb/guides/sharing-the-serial-console.md -- the flash contention is resolved because flashing no longer touches the UART. Cross-link serial-open-resets-esp32.

title: Robotics rover to Home Assistant (future)
description: Future third project: a controllable moving rover that exposes telemetry and non-realtime controls to Home Assistant through the same esphome-api registry (Switch, Number, Cover, sensor telemetry). The shared foundation (std esp-idf, hexagonal domain behind ports, native-API telemetry) does not preclude this. IMPORTANT divergence: the M5StickC Plus is NOT a flight controller (ESP32-PICO-D4 with a single MPU6886 IMU, no magnetometer or barometer, and HA is the wrong control path for flight). Keep any real-time control loop local to the firmware, keep telemetry/config on the native-API path, and expect different hardware for the eventual ArduPilot-style flight phase. Not designed yet; a placeholder to hold the roadmap so the foundation is not wired to require HA in the control path.
